about_role:
The Department of Public Works, Roads and Infrastructure (Limpopo) is offering an internship in Graduate Internship Programme 2027/2029. The stipend is R8,174 a month.

How to apply: Applicants should apply through the following website https://erecruitment.limpopo.gov.za. The application on the eRecruitment system should be accompanied by the new Z83 and recent comprehensive CV. Failure to attach required documents will result in the application not being considered/disqualified. Successful Interns will be appointed for a period of 24 months commencing 01 April 2027 to 31 March 2029. Interns will receive a monthly stipend in accordance to the Department of Public Service and Administration’s Directive on Employment of Persons on Developmental Programmes in the Public Service. Applications may also be hand delivered/posted to: Department of Public Works, Roads and Infrastructure: Private Bag X9490, Polokwane, 0700 or hand delivered at Works Tower Building, No. 43 Church Street, Polokwane, 0699. For Capricorn District: Private Bag X9378, Polokwane, 0700 Or hand deliver at 15 Landros Mare street, next to Correctional Services. For Mopani District: Private Bag X576, Giyani, 0826 or hand deliver at 570 Parliamentary Building, Giyani. For Sekhukhune District: Private Bag X02, Chuenespoort, 0745 or hand deliver at Lebowakgomo Zone A, next to traffic department. For Vhembe District: Private Bag X2248, Sibasa, 0970 or hand deliver at Cnr. Traffic and Raluswielo Street, Sibasa. For Waterberg District: Private Bag X1028, Modimolle, 0510 or hand deliver at Cnr. Thabo Mbeki & Elias Motsoaledi Street.
Reference number to quote: S.5/8/1/3/1
Closing date: 06 November 2026 at 16h30
Use the new Z83 form and attach a detailed CV.
requirements:
Study Field:
N Dip/Degree in Real Estate/B.Eng
Property Science and N Dip/Degree in Geographic Information Systems (GIS)

responsibilities:

Prevent, combat and investigate crime
Maintain public order
Protect and secure the inhabitants of the Republic and their property
Uphold and enforce the law.
requirements:
A person who applies to be employed as an entry level police trainee must - Apply on the form determined by the National Commissioner and affirm under oath or by way of a solemn declaration that the particulars furnished in the application, are the truth and correct
Be a citizen of the Republic of South Africa of which documentary proof must be furnished
Be at least eighteen (18) years of age and not older than thirty-five (35) years of age at the time of the closing date for applications stipulated in the relevant advertisement, of which documentary proof must be furnished
Submit himself or herself to a physical and medical examination as determined by the National Commissioner and must be found to be physically, medically and mentally fit for appointment in the service
Undergo a psychological and integrity assessment as determined by the National Commissioner and be found to comply with the profile of a police official
Be in possession of a grade 12 school certificate or equivalent qualification of which documentary proof must be furnished
Be proficient in at least English and one other official language
Be prepared to take the oath of office
Be prepared to undergo such training as, where and when determined by the National Commissioner
Not have any tattoo marks which will be visible when wearing any uniform of the Service
Not have been declared unfit to possess a firearm
Not have any previous criminal convictions or any pending criminal cases
Not have been dismissed for serious misconduct from the employ of a previous employer, where such dismissal relates to any act of dishonesty or violence; sexual harassment or is drug related
Allow a buccal sample and his or her fingerprints to be taken and verified against the criminal record system
Allow background enquiries to be made
Be prepared to undergo security vetting and obtain the level of security clearance determined by the National Commissioner; and Be prepared to serve anywhere in the Republic.
Applicants in possession of a relevant three (3) years tertiary qualification (NQF 6 or higher) i.e. Criminal Law / Policing / Forensic investigation etc.
Applicants in possession of other three (3) years tertiary qualification (NQF 6 or higher
Applicants in possession of Grade 12 school certificate with the minimum requirements for admission to bachelor’s degree
All applicants will be subjected to a fitness, psychometric and integrity testing as well as medical evaluation and will be interviewed during the recruitment, selection and enlistment process. The SAPS will also verify the qualifications, drivers’ licence, where applicable, citizenship and residential address of each applicant.
Applicants will be subjected to a vetting process which will include security screening, reference checking, social media presence and fingerprint verification to establish whether any illicit activity has been recorded or is pending against candidates.
Applicants who previously served in a Government Department and who were dismissed because of misconduct will not be considered for appointment in the South African Police Service (SAPS).
In view of the physical demands of the Basic Police Development Learning Programme, applicants with chronic diseases, physical impairments or any other health condition that may lead to interruption of the training programme, may be excluded from participation in the programme. Should applicants fail to disclose any health condition it may result in their withdrawal from the programme on the determination thereof.

Chef Directorate: Immovable Asset Management

How to apply: To apply for the below position, please apply online at https://jobs.gauteng.gov.za
Reference number to quote: REFS/056825
Closing date: 09 November 2026
Use the new Z83 form and attach a detailed CV.
responsibilities:
Oversee the design, implementation and maintenance of the Immovable Asset Strategy and Register and related asset management systems.
Oversee the preparation and annual review of the Custodian Asset Management Plan and its alignment with User Asset Management Plans and provincial planning and budget priorities.
Guide user departments on GIAMA planning requirements and consolidate their validated long-term asset needs into the provincial portfolio strategy.
Oversee the provision, integration and maintenance of Geographic Information System (GIS) services and spatial data for planning and decision-making.
Oversee asset-register verification standards, reconciliation and audit evidence, incorporate field information supplied by Facilities and Estate Management and technical teams and resolve discrepancies in property records.
Oversee GIAMA implementation, custodial policies and asset-management procedures, and monitor compliance across the provincial immovable asset portfolio.
Develop lifecycle portfolio strategies and prioritized investment proposals aligned with the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework and service-delivery requirements.
Oversee vesting and confirmation of custodianship, resolving ownership discrepancies with relevant authorities and maintaining supporting records.
Oversee property valuations and market analysis to inform acquisition, disposal and development decisions.
Set portfolio performance measures and report on utilisation, asset value, lifecycle costs and service-delivery outcomes, recommend corrective investment or rationalisation decisions.
Oversee asset recognition, derecognition, valuation and disclosure information in consultation with the CFO under the accounting framework applicable to the Department.
Oversee reconciliation of the immovable asset register with Deeds and Surveyor- General records and relevant financial information, resolve exceptions and asset-register audit findings.
Use condition-assessment information supplied by Facilities and Estate Management and technical teams to prioritise lifecycle investment, renewal and disposal in the custodial plan.
Oversee electronic asset-register development, data quality and controlled data exchange with GIS, user asset plans and relevant departmental systems.
Oversee the implementation of approved acquisition plans in line with accommodation needs and strategic objectives.
Oversee the implementation of approved disposal plans in line with legislative requirements, departmental policies and approved delegations.
Oversee the identification, assessment and evaluation of immovable properties for acquisition, disposal or alternative utilisation.
Oversee ad hoc acquisition requests and assessment of feasibility, affordability and compliance requirements.
Oversee the donation, transfer and land exchange of immovable assets.
Oversee the mitigation of risks associated with functionally obsolete immovable assets through ongoing assessment and measures aimed at preventing unforeseen and wasteful investments.
Oversee the undertaking of investment analysis and feasibility assessments for property development and infrastructure-related initiatives.
Oversee the identification and assessment of property development opportunities to optimise utilsation and value of immovable assets.
Oversee partnership and stakeholder engagements relating to property development initiatives, including intergovernmental and private sector collaborations.
Oversee the implementation and monitoring of Public Private Partnerships (PPPs) and other alternative service delivery mechanisms.
Oversee the development of policies, strategies, and plans for the Immovable Assets Management unit.
Oversee the alignment of the unit’s strategic priorities and work plans with those of the Department.
Oversee the preparation of the annual operation plan.
Oversee the identification of risks and implementation of risk and mitigation plans.
Oversee the preparation and presentation of management reports for the unit.
Oversee written contributions to departmental quarterly progress reports, Annual Report, SCOPA, Budget speeches, Annual Performance Plan, etc. Sign performance agreements for subordinates based on approved Job Descriptions, Strategic and Annual Performance Plans of the Department.
Manage subordinates and maintain discipline.
Manage the mentoring, coaching and professional development of subordinates for performance enhancement and succession planning support.
Manage talent retention and employee development initiatives.
Manage training and development of subordinates according to agreed training interventions.
Develop and update the service delivery and work plan for subordinates.
Manage funds in the unit in compliance with Public Finance Management Act and the Treasury Regulations.
Limit under spending or overspending by the unit in terms of the departmental budget allocations.
requirements:
An undergraduate qualification at NQF level 7 in Real Estate/Property Management/Property Development/Immovable Asset Management as recognized by SAQA.
At least 5 years’ experience at senior managerial level in the real estate environment.
A valid driver’s license.
A Pre-Entry SMS Certificate (Nyukela) submitted prior to appointment.
Competencies:
Knowledge of PFMA/Treasury Regulations
GIAMA planning, lifecycle investment analysis, property valuation, vesting and asset information governance
Provincial/Departmental Supply Chain Management Policies
Public Service Act of 1994 and Public Service Regulations, 2016, as amended
Government Immovable Asset Management Act of 2007
Labour Relations Act of 1995/Resolutions of Public Sector Bargaining Councils
Basic Conditions of Employment Act, 1997
Spatial Planning and Land Use Management Act, 2013
Provincial Infrastructure Delivery Management System
Gauteng Land Administration Act, 1996, as amended
Project Management, People Management, Financial Management and Conflict Management
Skills:
Communication
Report writing
Analytical
Negotiation
Facilitation and presentation
Attributes- Self-Driven, responsible, team player, resilient, innovative and adaptable

responsibilities:
The incumbent is responsible for the effective management of soft services within the departmental property portfolio, and in that capacity conducts site visits and condition assessments to determine soft service requirements.
The incumbent ensures that all facilities are maintained at habitable and hygienic standards, fit for occupation and for the purposes for which they are used.
The incumbent manages the delivery of cleaning and hygiene services in compliance with contractual specifications, service level agreements, the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 (Act 85 of 1993) and its regulations, and applicable public health requirements.
The incumbent also manages waste removal, grounds maintenance and gardening services in compliance with the National Environmental Management Act, 1998 (Act 107 of 1998), the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, 2008 (Act 59 of 2008) and applicable municipal by-laws, including the lawful handling, segregation, storage, removal and disposal of general and hazardous waste.
Pest control and fumigation programmes are implemented in accordance with approved schedules and applicable legislation, including the use of duly registered operators and approved products and the safe handling of hazardous chemical substances.
The incumbent maintains and updates project and facility information for all sites under the unit’s management.
The incumbent ensures that all equipment used by staff is in good functional, safe and serviceable condition, that statutory inspections and certification requirements are met, and that equipment is operated by competent persons.
Repairs are managed so that defects are attended to timeously and within approved budgets, with priority given to defects that compromise health, safety, hygiene or environmental compliance.
The incumbent plans and liaises with Supply Chain Management and Director Facilities Maintenance and for the timeous procurement of the consumables, supplies and spares required and service providers in compliance with the applicable procurement prescripts and with due regard to safety data requirements and environmentally responsible specifications.
At a strategic and planning level, the incumbent provides inputs into the development of soft services and maintenance policies, strategies and plans, and manages the preparation of the unit’s annual operational plan.
The incumbent oversees the implementation of risk management and mitigation plans, which include occupational health and safety, environmental and hygiene risks, and monitors service providers’ compliance with their statutory obligations, including health and safety plans, risk assessments, incident reporting and the provision of appropriate personal protective equipment.
The incumbent manages the preparation and presentation of management reports on soft services performance, on compliance with occupational health and safety, environmental and hygiene requirements, and on the maintenance and repair of equipment.
In respect of people management, the incumbent concludes performance agreements with subordinates, aligned to approved job descriptions and the Department’s Strategic and Annual Performance Plans.
The incumbent manages subordinates and maintains discipline in accordance with the applicable labour relations prescripts.
The incumbent also manages their training and development in accordance with agreed developmental interventions, including training required for statutory compliance in health and safety, and develops and updates their service delivery and work plans.
The incumbent promotes a safe working environment for staff and service providers’ employees in terms of the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993.
Regarding appointment of service providers, the official to prepare specifications for procurement of outsourced services and manage contracts with appointed service providers within applicable policies and Treasury prescripts.
Finally, the incumbent manages the unit’s funds in compliance with the Public Finance Management Act, 1999 and the Treasury Regulations, and limits under-expenditure and over-expenditure in accordance with the departmental budget allocations.

location: Dr George Mukhari Facility Maintenance Hub
about_role:
The Department of Infrastructure Development (Gauteng) is hiring a Construction Health and Safety Officer, based in Dr George Mukhari Facility Maintenance Hub. This is a permanent post, paying R338,106 a year.
Chief Directorate Maintenance

How to apply: To apply for the below position, please apply online at https://jobs.gauteng.gov.za
Reference number to quote: REFS/056875
Closing date: 09 November 2026
Use the new Z83 form and attach a detailed CV.
responsibilities:
Conduct site research and use trends analysis to identify system deficiencies and incident trends and outline relevant improvements.
Prepare health and safety specifications for construction sites and approve project specific health and safety plans.
Complete site establishment health and safety checklists.
Review and update health and safety plans.
Facilitate health and safety regular site, technical and progress meetings.
Compile project specific emergency response and preparedness plans and test the effectiveness.
Provide guidance to the establishment of the Departmental OHS Committee.
Represent the district at Departmental OHS committee meetings.
Facilitate legal appointment letters for 16.2s, GMR 2.1S and OHS Committees’ Chairpersons.
Provide demarcations and warning signs in areas where construction or maintenance operations are conducted.
Propose and execute remedial solutions for safety related issues on sites.
Attend the contractor’s site handover.
Conduct hazard identification and risk assessment processes (included in the health and safety specifications of the department or the contractor) for work activities on sites.
Inspect contractors’ equipment and file reports.
Monitor contractors executing construction works which are not in accordance with the approved Health and Safety plans.
Conduct baseline risk assessments/task specific risk assessment for the department.
Conduct emergency evacuation drills in all facilities.
Develop OHS Files for different facilities.
Participate in management reviews of the health and safety systems.
Identify training for staff and contractors on all OHS aspects.
Facilitate and conduct health and safety awareness session for staff and contractors at the district on health and safety procedures, firefighting, and disaster evacuations.
Act as a liaison between workers, management and subcontractors to ensure safety obligations are understood.
Maintain records of safety inspections, incidents and training.
Develop technical reports on health and safety issues and present findings to decision-makers.
requirements:
An undergraduate qualification at NQF 6 as recognised by SAQA in Safety Management.
At least 1-2 years’ experience in Safety Management.
A training in SAMTRAC, ISO 45001, HIRA, Incident Investigation, First Aid, Fire Fighting and Evacuation Coordination is required.
A valid driver’s license.
Competencies:
Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Act and its Regulations and environmental legislation (Construction Health and Safety)
Health and safety management systems and the key components of an effective system
Principles of cause and effect and its application to hazard identification and risk management on a project
Criteria and standards for effective documentation and documents control
Skills:
Computer literacy
Problem solving and analysis
Decision making
Creativity
Customer focus and responsiveness
Planning and organizing
Conflict management
Attributes: Reliable and Team player.

location: District Maintenance Hub Tshwane Mechanical Services
about_role:
The Department of Infrastructure Development (Gauteng) is hiring a Boiler Operator in Maintenance, based in District Maintenance Hub Tshwane Mechanical Services. This is a permanent post, paying R201,093.

How to apply: To apply for the below position, please apply online at https://jobs.gauteng.gov.za
Reference number to quote: REFS/056866
Closing date: 09 November 2026
Use the new Z83 form and attach a detailed CV.
responsibilities:
Request chemicals from stores as required.
Test quality of water of softeners as well as the returning flows of condensate water.
Fill chemicals tank with required chemicals as prescribed.
Top up salt in brine tank.
Check working conditions of chemical pumps.
Test total dissolve solids (TDS) and blow-down according to prescripts.
Monitor the stream pressure constantly Check correct temperature of hot well tanks.
Adjust the stoker for efficient steam delivery.
Report all defects immediately.
Check the feed water pump-levels and hot well tanks for sufficient water supply to the boiler.
Ensure that standby boilers and funnel is full of water and chemicals at all times.
Control the flow of fuel.
Ensure that the boiler environment is well maintained.
Ensure proper usage of protective clothing.
Ensure that the boiler environment is clean and safe.
Ensure that the brine tank and water filter are cleaned as prescribed.
Ensure the removal of ash from boilers, gritt arrester and smoke box.
Log all recordings as per the assessment in the logbook.
Perform supervisory functions.
Receive and signoff on the delivery of coal.
Provide shift reports.
Maintenance of shift/overtime register.
Perform related adhoc duties.
requirements:
Grade 10 and an equivalent recognized National Steam Certificate.
At least 1 year appropriate hands-on experience gained in boiler operating.
Competencies:
Basic knowledge of norms and standards on low pressure
Knowledge of Maintenance Works Norms and Standards
Knowledge of maintenance tools
Knowledge of Occupational Health and Safety Act
Skills:
Interpersonal relations
Ability to utilise Public Works maintenance tools
Planning and organising
Staff supervision
Communication (written & verbal)
Attributes:
People centred
Professionalism
Collective responsibility
Transformation
Batho Pele Principles
Attention to detail
Honesty and integrity
Strong ethics

Insight into local healthcare delivery, diversity, transformation and equity.

The Key Purpose of this role is to work towards achieving growth in volumes sold growth in market share and increased competitiveness through providing market driven differentiated service that builds sustainable competitiveness within clearly identified segments.
responsibilities:
Achieve sales targets for assigned areas
Manage and supervise Distributors of assigned sector (order, payment, re-distribution)
Ensure IB products are available in reasonable stock (complete range) in the customers and retail outlets
Ensure chiller are properly placed in the performing outlet and used exclusively for IBPLC products in the assigned sector
Monitor the recommended price of our product at sales outlets
Closely monitor actions of the competition
requirements:
3-year degree qualification
At least 2 years' experience in sales/marketing/FMCG environment
Valid unendorsed Cod 8 drivers' license
Basic computer literacy and experiencing working with Microsoft Office
Local area knowledge is a requirement
Excellent administration skills

SAB is hiring a Business Development Manager, based in SAB Ottery Depot.

responsibilities:
Build and maintain strong POC relationships and address any key points by working with different SAB teams (e.g. Brand Teams, Trade Marketing etc) ensuring the highest level of customer service
Manage customer expectation and ensure that their needs are met in a timely fashion
Develop and implement customer specific business programs and account plans
Develop new sales opportunities for Premium Beer
Educate and train customers on SABs Premium category to ensure correct in store positioning and execution of the brans to enhance the customer experience
Assist the Premium CO. Team to drive market share, meet financial targets and growth objectives for SAB Premium Brands in Key FOP outlets
Assist the Premium CO. Team to develop comprehensive brand plans for the Premium Category
Provide the Premium CO. Team with key customer insights on the super alcohol category to ensure category strategy alignment to customer needs
Key Attributes and Competencies:
Strong communication and interpersonal skills with aptitude for building relationships with key stakeholders at different levels
Relationship Management
Customer service
Strong negotiation skills
Problem solving
Entrepreneurial mindset with strong Commercial Acumen
Extensive knowledge of SABs Premium Category
Attention to detail
Highly professional
Ability to innovate and be creative when it comes to events and activities
Work well independently
Able to work outside of normal working hours
requirements:
Minimum 3-year tertiary qualification
3-5 years sales experience within FMCG
Valid drivers License (Essential )

The Baker’s Assistant supports the baker and bakery team with the preparation, production, baking, decorating, packaging, and presentation of baked goods. The role involves preparing ingredients, maintaining a clean and organised work area, assisting with equipment and baking processes, and ensuring that products meet the required quality and hygiene standards.
Grade 12 or equivalent qualification.

The Baker’s Assistant works closely with the baker to ensure the smooth and efficient daily operation of the bakery. Duties may include measuring and weighing ingredients, preparing doughs and mixtures, assisting with baking and decorating products, loading and unloading ovens, cooling and packaging finished products, and preparing orders for customers.
The successful candidate will also be responsible for cleaning and sanitising workstations, utensils, baking equipment, and storage areas. They must follow all food-safety and occupational-health-and-safety procedures and ensure that ingredients are stored correctly.
The role requires attention to detail, consistency, good time management, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment. The Baker’s Assistant should demonstrate a positive attitude, willingness to learn, and commitment to producing high-quality baked products while maintaining excellent standards of cleanliness and hygiene.

Heineken Beverages is hiring a Quality Assurance Manager, based in Johannesburg.
Lead site quality at HEINEKEN Beverages, putting consumers first and developing the people, processes and assurance systems that deliver First Time Right quality.
In this role, you will prevent food safety and quality failures through effective assurance systems, stable processes, well-maintained equipment and material integrity. Working with Cellars/Brewing, Production and Engineering, you will use reliable data to improve process capability, lead the Product Quality (PQ) pillar and drive continuous improvement, New Product Introduction (NPI) and incoming material quality. The role forms part of Supply Chain and reports to the Plant Manager / Brewery Manager.
Lead the site quality strategy in alignment with HEINEKEN standards, operating company (OpCo) priorities and consumer needs.
Identify and prevent food safety and quality risks through reliable data, compliant systems and effective process controls.
Build a consumer-first quality culture and operational ownership of First Time Right performance.
Lead the site PQ pillar and the shift towards quality at source and condition-based management.
Protect consumers, product integrity and the reputation of HEINEKEN Beverages through effective quality governance.
Maintain and improve integrated quality, food safety and laboratory management systems.
responsibilities:
Lead the site quality strategy and integrated assurance systems:
Implement a consumer-focused site quality vision and strategy covering processes, organisation and people development.
Maintain and improve integrated quality, food safety and laboratory management systems, procedures, checklists and standards.
Build a strong quality culture across all site functions, working with OpCo Quality and Global Supply Chain and sharing learning across sites and operating companies.
Lead the PQ pillar, quality at source and continuous improvement:
Lead the site PQ pillar, establish and maintain Quality Factors and Q-Points, and develop autonomous teams to sustain quality conditions.
Apply advanced Unified Problem Solving to prevent recurring failures, improve First Time Right, reduce losses and work towards zero quality defects.
Support corrective and preventive actions and transfer PQ tasks to Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Planned Maintenance (PM), building Production ownership of quality and release within agreed standards.
Lead measurement management to ensure accurate, reliable and timely results, supporting operational teams with troubleshooting, calibration and equipment verification.
Analyse product and process data to identify risks and improve process capability. Where capability and controls are established, shift the emphasis from finished-product testing to process and condition control, particularly hygiene.
Embed lean quality-at-source systems and identify cost and value improvement opportunities across processes, technologies, recipes and materials. Support benchmarking and provide expert technological guidance.
Develop quality champions and process-owner capability for routine analysis. Production / Brewing is responsible for satellite laboratories and sampling, excluding microbiological sampling; Quality provides technical support.
Protect product integrity and HEINEKEN Beverages’ reputation:
Align site stakeholders with HEINEKEN policies and applicable legislation governing food safety and product integrity.
Monitor customer and consumer feedback, manage complaint investigations and verify the effectiveness of corrective and preventive actions.
Support supplier performance monitoring for raw, packaging and auxiliary materials through operational feedback, verification of corrective actions and supplier collaboration.
Lead site New Product Introduction:
Lead site NPI implementation within the stage-gate model. Provide quality input into technological and legislative assessments and the approval of raw, auxiliary and packaging materials and production processes.
Apply project management and Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) to ensure food safety, conformance, quality and delivery on time and in full.
Lead people development and cross-functional capability:
Build quality control, assurance and food safety skills through training, continuous learning and awareness activities.
Plan shifts, overtime and temporary labour to meet changing demand and maintain effective quality support.
Attract, recruit, develop and retain talent.
Develop end-to-end specialists and encourage knowledge sharing across manufacturing sites and operating companies.
Manage individual and team performance, fostering engagement, collaboration and cross-functional integration.
Build process-owner autonomy in advanced problem solving and defect analysis to sustain food safety, quality and reliable delivery.
Manage departmental budgets and costs:
Develop annual operating expenditure (OPEX) and capital expenditure (CAPEX) budgets and business plans for the end-to-end quality assurance roadmap, including process-control equipment and consumables.
Implement approved plans, monitor monthly expenditure and follow up on variances. Approve goods and services within budget and delegated authority, and plan resources for unexpected demand peaks.
Embed safety, food safety and sustainability:
Embed health and safety in QA workflows, laboratories and associated facilities, including equipment safety checks before use.
Integrate food safety into operations and NPI. Use safety data and consumer feedback to drive continuous improvement and help ensure products are fit for consumption.
Contribute to HEINEKEN’s Brewing a Better World sustainability objectives through departmental plans and daily practices.
Manage information and quality reporting:
Report weekly and monthly results, significant incidents, trends and business impact covering food safety, product quality, supplier performance and consumer insights.
Maintain and improve reporting systems and use data to guide decisions and improve process stability. Monitor applicable measures including PQI, FTR, losses, CVE, NPI delivery, Taste Test Score, OPEX, customer and consumer complaints, supplier performance and system improvement.
Role Requirements:
Minimum bachelor’s degree in Food Technology, Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Microbiology or Chemical Engineering.
Experience in quality control, quality assurance and food safety management systems.
People management and leadership experience, with the ability to lead and develop teams.
Minimum 10 years’ experience in food and/or beverage production and production technology.
Experience in laboratory operations within food and beverage production, together with brewing / packaging experience.
Ability to communicate effectively in English and collaborate across functions.
Experience applying continuous improvement methodologies such as TPM, Lean or Six Sigma, with strong problem-solving and facilitation skills.
Planning and project management experience; exposure to Utilities and New Product Introduction (NPI) is preferred.
Strong data analysis, measurement management and process performance management capabilities.
Core Skills Required:
People leadership, organisational development and cross-functional collaboration.
Quality assurance, quality systems and standards, safety and sustainability.
Strategy development, implementation and excellence in execution.
Financial planning, cost control and value creation.
Advanced problem solving and process performance improvement.
Data management, digitalisation and evidence-based decision-making.

job_title: Vice President: Internal Controls - Financial Reporting
about_role:
AECI is hiring a Vice President: Internal Controls - Financial Reporting, based in Sandton.
To provide strategic leadership, governance, and oversight of the Group's Internal Financial Controls (IFC) framework, ensuring compliance with JSE Listing Requirements (Section 3.84(k)), the COSO 2013 framework, and applicable governance standards. The role is responsible for strengthening the control environment across the Group, safeguarding the integrity of financial reporting, managing financial reporting risks, driving continuous improvement in control effectiveness, and providing assurance to executive leadership and the Audit & Risk Committee on the adequacy and effectiveness of internal financial controls.
responsibilities:
JSE 3.84(k) Compliance Leadership and Oversight:
Lead the planning, execution, and management of the company’s Internal Financial Controls (IFC) compliance program to meet JSE Listings Requirements (specifically Section 3.84(k)), ensuring timely and effective completion of reporting cycles.
Support the Group Chief Financial Officer in driving continuous improvement in the IFC program maturity, scalability, and risk coverage in alignment with the King V Report on Corporate Governance.
Risk and Control Assessment:
Oversee the scoping, risk assessment, and control identification process for all Business Units and Group functions in collaboration with key stakeholders, including Group Risk and Group Internal Audit, for final approval by the Group Chief Financial Officer.
Evaluate new risks, with the support of Group Risk, arising from organisational changes, acquisitions, systems implementations, or regulatory updates (e.g., Companies Act of South Africa, governance changes, tax regulations in various jurisdictions etc.).
Internal Control Design and Testing:
Ensure proper design and implementation of internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR/IFC), focusing on key controls that will ensure high assurance coverage levels for all financial balances included in the primary financial statements (i.e., Statement of Financial Position; Statement of Comprehensive Income, Statement of Changes in Equity, and Statement of Cash Flow).
Proper design and implementation of Group controls, including, Entity-level Controls (ELCs), IT General Controls (ITGCs), and Fraud controls.
Proper design and implementation of business/operational controls, including manual and automated controls.
Manage the control testing strategy, including Management control self-assessment reported through the Internal Control Matrix (ICM) process, Group Internal Audit assurance as part of the Combined Assurance Model, and External Audit assurance.
Ensure timely remediation of deficiencies identified through the ICM, Combined Assurance, and External Audit processes.
Stakeholder Engagement and Communication:
Serve as a key liaison with External Audit, Group Internal Audit, Group and Business Finance, and Group IT to align on testing, controls reliance, and remediation.
Provide clear and timely communication to senior leadership and control owners on IFC matters, including deficiencies and remediation plans.
Provide assistance with the resolution of control queries/deficiencies in all regions/countries in which the Group operations as well as within Group Functions.
Ensure timeous escalation of unresolved deficiencies and incomplete documentation supporting IFC’s to the Group Chief Financial Officer for corrective action.
Governance and Reporting:
Maintain sound relationships with Group Chief Executive Officer, Group Chief Financial Officer, Audit & Risk Committee and other Group Functions with regards to IFCs.
Prepare and present regular updates to the Group Chief Executive Officer, Group Chief Financial Officer, and the Audit & Risk Committee on JSE 3.84(k) compliance status, key findings, and emerging risks.
Final review and sign-off on bottom-up collection of control evidence of Management self-assessments informing ICM submissions and reporting.
Maintain documentation standards and oversee control certifications and sub-certification processes required to support the Group Chief Executive Officer and Group Chief Financial Officer's statutory sign-off requirements in terms of the JSE 3.84(k) requirements.
Team Leadership and Development:
Provide continuous training and awareness to all control owners as and when required. This may include ad-hoc travel to regions and jurisdiction to provide face-to-face training.
Manage and mentor a team of IFC professionals, providing guidance, feedback, and development opportunities (currently no team - the size of the team will be determined based on the outcome of the Internal Controls of Financial Reporting Project).
Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Process and Technology Optimisation:
Identify opportunities to leverage technology, automation, and data analytics to enhance control effectiveness and program efficiency.
Continuously focus on moving from manual to automated controls, thereby reducing dependency on manual controls.
Drive alignment with broader internal control and governance initiatives, including ESG and overall enterprise risk management (ERM), where relevant, in collaboration with the functional teams responsible for ESG and ERM.
requirements:

FirstRand is hiring an Integrated Scenario Analyst, based in Johannesburg.
To support the development, implementation, and ongoing embedding of the Group’s integrated scenario analysis capability within FirstRand Group Treasury. The role applies risk, finance, and quantitative expertise to analyse complex data, develop and code quantitative models, and produce insightful dashboards that inform strategic decision‑making, capital planning, and risk management.
The role operates within a dynamic, intellectually challenging environment that requires continuous learning and capability development, while collaborating with stakeholders across the Group and across multiple industries, including banking, insurance, and investments, to enhance and mature the Group’s integrated scenario analysis capability.
Understand and apply scenario formulation techniques to evaluate the impact of economic, financial, and operational scenarios on the Group’s performance, resource allocation, liquidity, and capital planning.
Lead and support the expansion and embedding of the integrated scenario analysis capability across multiple use cases, including ICAAP stress testing, common scenario stress testing, FRM, budget‑lite processes, and other strategic applications.
Conduct and lead research into scenario design, macro‑financial linkages, and risk drivers, incorporating internal and external data, regulatory expectations, and industry best practice.
Build, enhance, review, and challenge quantitative scenario methodologies and models, working collaboratively with Risk, Finance, Treasury, and relevant subject matter experts (SMEs).
Develop, code, and maintain quantitative models and analytical tools, ensuring robustness, transparency, scalability, and appropriate governance.
Perform data preparation, validation, and analysis, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and consistency of inputs used in scenario modelling and reporting.
Review, interpret, and analyse scenario outputs, ensuring results are conceptually sound, analytically coherent, and decision‑useful.
Ensure scenario results are reported in line with relevant internal standards, regulatory requirements, and accounting frameworks, and that outputs reconcile back to regulatory returns and financial statements.
Design and maintain dashboards and management information to communicate scenario results, key drivers, sensitivities, and insights effectively.

Support methodology documentation, governance processes, and audit readiness, including responding to internal and external review queries.
Monitor and adapt scenarios in response to changing economic conditions, regulatory developments, and emerging risks.
Act as a collaborative partner across the Group, working with stakeholders across banking, insurance, and investment businesses to ensure alignment and consistency of scenario analysis.
Contribute to the continuous improvement and maturity of the Group’s integrated scenario analysis capability through innovation, automation, and ongoing skills development.

about_role:
Heineken Beverages is hiring an Automation Engineer, based in Johannesburg.
The key purpose of this role is to provide structured, strategic and leadership within the automation and control discipline across Heineken Beverages manufacturing operations. The role develops and governs automation standards, architecture, frameworks and lifecycle practices; influences site and project decisions; improves manufacturing reliability and performance; strengthens PCD cybersecurity; and enables the controlled implementation and enhancement of digital manufacturing technologies. The role works across sites and functions to ensure automation solutions are safe, reliable, maintainable, secure, integrated, scalable and aligned with Heineken requirements and long-term business priorities.
responsibilities:
Automation Manufacturing Reliability and Continuous Improvement:
Provide cross-site technical leadership to improve the reliability, maintainability and performance of automation and control systems.
Establish and govern reliability standards, maintenance strategies and performance measures for PLC, SCADA, HMI, industrial networks, drives, instrumentation and associated control infrastructure.
Analyse systemic failures, repeat breakdowns and automation-related production losses; lead structured root cause analysis and ensure sustainable corrective and preventive actions are implemented.
Support sites with complex or high-impact automation incidents while strengthening site capability and ownership.
Identify and prioritise opportunities to improve throughput, quality, energy performance, process stability, OPI and cost through automation and advanced control.
Develop reusable troubleshooting practices, standard diagnostics, technical guidance and lessons-learned mechanisms across the manufacturing network.
Automation Projects and Obsolescence Management:
Provide technical assurance and lifecycle governance for automation capital projects, upgrades and obsolescence programmes.
Define automation project requirements, design principles, acceptance criteria and handover standards.
Review and approve control philosophies, functional design specifications, architectures, software designs, network designs and supplier proposals for compliance with approved standards.
Participate in design reviews, risk assessments, FAT, SAT, commissioning, performance verification and operational handover for strategic projects.
Develop and maintain automation asset lifecycle and obsolescence frameworks, site risk profiles, technology roadmaps and prioritised replacement plans.
Automation Technology, Architecture and Integration:
Define and govern fit-for-purpose automation technologies and integration patterns across the control and manufacturing landscape.
Own and maintain reference architectures, approved technology standards, software libraries, naming conventions, interface principles and engineering practices for automation and control systems.
Evaluate emerging and existing technologies against business value, cybersecurity, interoperability, supportability, scalability and lifecycle requirements.
Ensure reliable integration between field devices, control systems, SCADA, historians, MES, utilities platforms, reporting solutions and approved enterprise services.
Guide industrial communication and data integration using approved protocols, segmented architectures and clearly defined ownership boundaries between OT and IT.
Maintain strategic relationships with OEMs, system integrators and technology partners; influence roadmaps and ensure solutions remain aligned with Heineken architecture and support models.
Create governance mechanisms for deviations, technical decisions, solution assurance and controlled introduction of new technology.
PCD Cybersecurity and Compliance:
Strengthen cybersecurity and compliance within the Process Control Domain through standards, risk management and technical governance.
Translate Heineken PCD security requirements into practical automation engineering standards, implementation roadmaps and assurance controls.
Govern secure network segmentation, access control, remote access, backup and restore, patching, malware protection, account management, logging and recovery practices for automation assets.
Support PCD risk assessments, audits, vulnerability remediation and incident response, ensuring actions are prioritised according to operational and business risk.
Embed security-by-design into automation projects, system changes, supplier access and technology lifecycle decisions.
Define evidence, documentation and compliance routines required to demonstrate that controls are implemented, sustained and periodically tested.
Collaborate with PCD Security, IT, site engineering and external partners to resolve risks without compromising safety, quality or production continuity.
Digital Manufacturing Implementation and Enhancement:
Enable sustainable digital manufacturing solutions by ensuring robust automation data foundations, controlled integration and measurable operational value.
Provide automation leadership for historian, MES, OPI, energy, condition monitoring, analytics and other approved digital manufacturing initiatives.
Define data acquisition, contextualisation, tag, interface, time synchronisation, data quality and ownership standards from shop-floor systems to authorised digital platforms.
Ensure digital solutions are industrialised, supportable, cybersecure and integrated into site operating and maintenance routines rather than remaining isolated pilots.
Partner with operations, engineering, digital, data and IT teams to translate business problems into scalable automation and data solutions.
Assess solution performance after implementation and drive enhancements based on adoption, reliability, data quality and realised business benefits.
Standards, Governance, Capability and Strategic Influence:
Build a consistent and sustainable automation engineering capability across Heineken Beverages through governance, assurance and knowledge leadership.
Develop, maintain and deploy automation policies, standards, frameworks, specifications, templates and technical procedures aligned with global and local requirements.
Establish governance forums, compliance assessments, maturity reviews and performance reporting to provide visibility of automation risks, priorities and progress.
Influence investment plans and management decisions by presenting clear technical risk, lifecycle, cost and business-impact information.
Provide coaching, technical mentoring and structured capability development for site automation engineers, technicians, project engineers and relevant stakeholders.
Facilitate cross-site communities of practice, knowledge sharing, benchmarking and replication of proven solutions.
Define competency expectations and support succession and training for the automation and control discipline.
Act as a recognised subject matter expert and escalation point, balancing enterprise standardisation with site requirements and operational realities.
Safety, Health, Environment and Quality:
Ensure that automation strategies, designs, changes and work practices protect people, product, plant, information and the environment.
Apply management-of-change, functional safety, quality, environmental and legal requirements to automation engineering activities.
Ensure control system modifications are appropriately assessed, tested, approved, documented, backed up and recoverable before release to production.
Promote safe engineering behaviours and ensure suppliers and partners comply with site and Heineken SHE requirements.
requirements:
Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Mechatronics, Process Control, Instrumentation, Automation or a related engineering discipline.
Relevant professional registration, postgraduate qualification or recognized automation, industrial networking, cybersecurity or project certification would be an added advantage.
Minimum 10 years relevant experience in industrial automation and control within a manufacturing or process environment, including experience with PLC, SCADA/HMI, industrial networks, drives, instrumentation and system integration.
Demonstrated experience in automation projects, reliability improvement, technology lifecycle or obsolescence management and cross-functional technical leadership.
Experience operating across multiple manufacturing sites, developing standards or providing technical governance at business, regional or Centre of Excellence level would be an added advantage.

Only a detailed CV should be attached to your application form. Only shortlisted candidates will be required to submit certified copies not older than 6 months of qualifications and other related documents on or before the day of the interview. Applicants must note that further checks will be conducted once they are shortlisted and that their appointment is subject to positive outcomes on these checks, which include security clearance, security vetting, qualification verification and criminal records verification. Candidates must comply with the minimum appointment requirements. CV’s should be aligned to reflect one’s degree of compliance with the advertisement requirements and responsibilities. The Department of Correctional Services reserves the right not to fill these posts. Persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply. Candidates must comply with the minimum appointment requirements. CV’s should be aligned to reflect one’s degree of compliance with the advertisement requirements and responsibilities. The Department of Correctional Services reserves the right not to fill these posts.
responsibilities:
Analyse and critically evaluate information in order to identify continuing risk/dangerous-ness in an individual offender’s case, where information may come from a variety of sources including electronic and paper documents, electronic updates and evidence given at oral hearings.
Apply knowledge and judgement to offenders’ cases in order to decide whether they can safely be released into the community and to set conditions where release is appropriate.
Oversee the hearing of cases in order to assess risk.
Work collaboratively with other parole members in order to make judgements about the available evidence and to provide a concise and structured summary of relevant factors in reaching a decision or recommendation.
Facilitate report writing, draft reasoned summaries and decisions.
Be an effective ambassador for the Parole Board when representing it at hearings or any other event.
Facilitate administrative roles associated with preparation for hearings, hearings and revocations/cancellations, public education on parole, facilitate invitation of victims to hearings including court attendance as a result of litigation by offenders.
requirements:
A recognized and appropriate NQF level 7 qualification in any Criminal Justice field, Social Sciences or related.
Previous 5 years’ experience in management or decision-making position.
Demonstrable experience of and ability to conduct effective evidence-based decision making, weighing facts and evidence, analysing and critically evaluating large volumes of complex information and identifying key issues, within tight deadlines and working on your own initiative.
Demonstrable independence of mind and sound judgement, with the ability to make evidence-based decisions that are accurately documented.
Excellent interpersonal skills: The ability to gain respect and maintain rapport through effective communication and influencing skills - with the confidence to challenge opinions where necessary, work collegiately and resolve differences to reach sound decisions.
Excellent communication skills, both written and oral: The ability to communicate sensitively and effectively with a wide range of individuals, varying your approach as necessary and treating others with respect, to listen actively and evaluate replies in order to probe issues.
Excellent written skills: The ability to draft well-formed written reports which summarizes evidence in support of a decision or recommendation.
Demonstrable high standards of corporate and personal integrity and conduct, such as a strong commitment to fairness, equality and the ethos of supporting the wider public or community good through your contributions.
High levels of time management, organizational and administrative skills, together with strong personal motivation and commitment to professional self-development.
Evidence of experience of any aspect of the criminal justice system and an understanding of the importance of the victim’s perspective.
Previous experience in management or decision-making position.

responsibilities:
The Chairperson will be responsible for leading the Committee in advising the Accounting Officer in fulfilling their statutory responsibilities in terms of the Public Finance Management Act and other relevant prescripts as they relate to the following key areas: ICT Governance and Strategy: Leading the Committee in overseeing the development, implementation, and monitoring of the ICT Strategy and Enterprise Architecture, ensuring alignment with the strategic objectives.

Cybersecurity and Information Security: Steering the Committee’s oversight of robust cybersecurity and information security measures, including compliance with POPIA, MISS, and the National Cybersecurity Policy Framework, and managing ICT-related risks.
Service Delivery and Digital Transformation: Guiding the Committee’s monitoring of ICT service performance and reliability, championing digital transformation initiatives to improve service delivery, and overseeing the management of service level agreements (SLAs).

Ensuring the Committee’s oversight of the ICT environment complies with all relevant legislation, including the PFMA, SITA Act, ECT Act, and POPIA, as well as applicable National Treasury regulations and minimum ICT standards
In addition to the above, the Chairperson will be responsible for: Setting the agenda for Committee meetings
Chairing all Committee meetings, ensuring constructive dialogue and effective decision-making
Representing the Committee’s views and recommendations to the Accounting Officer
Acting as the primary liaison between the Committee, the Accounting Officer, and the Audit and Risk Management Committee on ICT governance matters.
requirements:

At least 10 years’ experience in senior management or executive leadership in ICT, with a portion of this experience preferably within the South African public sector.
Demonstrated expertise in ICT governance, strategy development, enterprise architecture, digital transformation, and the management of large-scale ICT projects.
In-depth knowledge and understanding of the South African ICT regulatory and policy landscape.
Professional membership and good standing status in relevant bodies is an added advantage.
In-depth knowledge of the PFMA and the Treasury Regulations, as well as other governing prescripts.
Exhibit independence of mind in deliberations and be proactive in advising the Accounting Officer.
Applicants may not be in the employment of the Department and must have no business or personal relationship with the Department.
